title: Natural selection turns slight varieties into more distinct ones and species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Natural selection turns slight varieties into more distinct ones and species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Individual differences lead to slight varieties, these to more distinct and permanent varieties, then to sub-species and species, the passage being mainly due to natural selection accumulating structural differences in definite directions, so that a well-marked variety is an incipient species.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I attribute the passage of a variety, from a state in which it differs very slightly from its parent to one in which it differs more, to the action of natural selection in accumulating (as will hereafter be more fully explained) differences of structure in certain definite directions.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter II, “Variation under Nature”; section “Doubtful species”. Scope: varieties and species in nature

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch02-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Many divergence continua can be analyzed with public genomic data, but they are snapshots and taxonomically biased. They test pathways in selected systems rather than the general progression asserted.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Use genomic and phenotypic time series of diverging populations to test whether selection progressively increases stable differentiation and reproductive isolation beyond drift and gene-flow models. Directional accumulation ending in isolation supports the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Selection and reduced gene flow can be difficult to separate.

Most speciation histories lack temporal observations.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.6
data existence: 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Sequence and tree archives can line up close forms into a divergence series, which proxies the descriptive half. They seldom include the fitness or selection measures needed to show that natural selection, rather than drift, accumulates the steps. The mechanistic ranking is therefore only partly testable, and only in complexes that happen to have both ranks and population genomics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Along phylogeographic series, test whether populations ranked as slight varieties, marked varieties, and species differ by increasing, directionally selected trait change rather than by drift-sized divergence. A graded series whose steps are enriched for selected loci would support natural selection as the main passage; series produced by isolation and drift alone would count against that attribution.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Incipient species' and 'definite directions' need a threshold that is not in the original wording.

Drift, founder events, and selection all produce stepped divergence.

Selection scans and variety ranks are rarely in the same public table outside a few model complexes.
